summary.headline: Stove Kraft Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 32.4% YoY to INR414.5 crore, with PAT of INR6.1 crore and EBITDA margin of 9.5%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 32.4% YoY to INR414.5 crore, driven by induction cooktops (15.5% of revenue, value up 89.4% YoY) and small appliances. Gross margin held at 38.6%, flat YoY, while EBITDA rose 33.9% to INR39.5 crore at a 9.5% margin. FY26 revenue grew 10.9% to INR1,607.4 crore and EBITDA margin was 10.3%, below the roughly 11% management says it aims to protect. Management guided to upwards of 15% revenue growth in FY27, citing small appliances, export recovery and IKEA billing from Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1.4 crore in Q4 FY25 (+317.8%)

financial_highlights.metric: Small kitchen appliances share of revenue (Q4)

financial_highlights.change: Up from 3.8% in Q3 (YTD basis per call); FY26 10.7%

segments.name: Induction cooktops
segments.commentary: Contributed 15.5% of Q4 revenue; value +89.4% and volume +67.3% YoY. Installed capacity about 2 million units last year, with current run-rate guided at 4-5 million units.

segments.name: Small kitchen appliances
segments.commentary: Contributed 40.2% of Q4 revenue; value +12.7% YoY versus volume +97.7%, which management attributed to a mix shift toward lower-ASP products.

segments.name: Pressure cookers / cookware
segments.commentary: Pressure cooker value grew 44% YoY in Q4; non-stick cookware grew 49% YoY on stronger exports. Management said aluminium-to-stainless steel premiumisation is lifting value.

segments.name: OEM exports
segments.commentary: Q4 share 8.7% of revenue; FY26 10.7%. Management expects exports to return to about 12% of revenue, with a U.S. tariff cut from about 50% to about 18% and customer price increases from 1 June.

segments.name: Retail (EBOs)
segments.commentary: 329 exclusive brand outlets at 31 March 2026, up 67 in FY26 (16 in Q4). Average sales per store rose to INR4.7 lakh from INR3.8 lakh; retail is about 9% of revenue. Target 500 stores by 2027, and about 25 stores added per quarter.

segments.name: IKEA (new)
segments.commentary: Three product lines awarded. Billing expected from Q1 FY27: about INR40-50 crore by year-end, and INR200-250 crore at full utilisation of the three lines.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at upwards of 15%, driven by small appliances, export normalisation and IKEA.
EBITDA margin: management aims to protect about 11% and improve from there. FY26 actual was 10.3%.
Gross margin: target improvement of about 1% per year, reaching about 42% within 2-3 years.
FY27 capex guided at about INR40 crore including retail. Management said net cash outflow for FY26 capex was about INR70-75 crore.
Working capital: management is confident of keeping working capital days in the 24-30 day range, and below 30 days.
Peak capacity with existing facilities estimated at INR2,500-3,000 crore revenue.
capex_capacity: Capex capitalised in FY26 was about INR109-111 crore on the cash flow statement, but this is funded largely by supplier credit; net cash outflow is about INR70-75 crore.
Substation for electric power and one IKEA plant remain as the only significant WIP items; the main capex cycle is complete.
Induction cooktop capacity was about 2 million units last year. Additional lines are being set up at Baddi, besides Bangalore, to reach 4-5 million units at current run-rate.
Manufacturing is 97-98% in-house. Management said the capex was designed for INR3,000 crore revenue capacity.
Retail network is expanding at about 25 stores per quarter, and the company is moving to COFO/FOFO models, with franchisee-operated stores expected to be the majority within 2 years.
demand_pricing: Management cited surging induction cooktop demand after the Iran war and geopolitical supply disruptions, and said demand is shifting from an emergency option to a daily-use appliance.
Price increases of about 10% were taken in the current quarter to pass on commodity costs; export customers agreed to increases from 1 June.
GST reduction to 5% on relevant products (mid-Q3) was cited as supporting organised-player demand.
Management said it is leader by volume in induction cooktops and pressure cookers on e-commerce, but gave no market share numbers.
Forex loss in Q4 was called a one-off impact; rupee depreciation is a margin headwind. Management said it expects to pass on commodity costs but not fully on forex.

qa_highlights.question: Why are capex and interest cash flows high, and why did the opex rise 41%?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex capitalised was about INR111 crore, partly funded by supplier credit (about INR32 crore). Interest rose on supplier credit and sale-and-leaseback, while borrowing costs fell. Management said freight, warranty, business promotion and sales commission grew in line with revenue; sales commission rose about INR10 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is EBITDA margin expected to rise above 11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims to protect about 11% and improve from there, with growth above 15% and any upside to margin. Q4 EBITDA margin was 9.5%, hit by one-off forex loss.

qa_highlights.question: How much capacity and capex is needed to double induction production?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity is about 2 million units now and run-rate is 4-5 million. Added capex is small (assembly and testing lines). FY27 capex is about INR40 crore including retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivables are largely channel-financed (most collected within 15 days), payables are on an invoice platform (paid in 90 days versus 45-day MSME terms), and it is confident of staying in the 24-30 day range. Aluminium and steel stock was built ahead of price rises.

qa_highlights.question: Are new stores accretive, and what is the same-store growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Average sales per store rose to INR4.7 lakh from INR3.8 lakh. Management said Q4 same-store growth was 25-30% for mature stores. Franchisee economics: INR2 lakh fixed fee plus 15-30% store margin; inventory stays on company books, funded by franchisee deposits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IKEA revenue ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Three product lines are awarded. Revenue begins Q1 FY27, with about INR40-50 crore before FY27 year-end and INR200-250 crore at full utilisation of all three lines.

risks_watch: Forex volatility and rupee depreciation, which management called a one-off Q4 hit and a challenge to pass on fully.
Q4 other expenses at about INR62 crore, up sharply with sales commission and freight; the call gave no quantification of the margin impact of retail mix.
Sustainability of the induction demand surge; the pipeline refill by peers could affect growth.
Import dependence on glass (33-40% of import content), PCBs and magnets for induction cooktops, with no domestic glass capacity.
Export recovery is gradual, and price increases were only agreed from 1 June.
Capex and cash flow disclosure: management said figures would be shared offline, and the net-of-supplier-credit figures were not fully reconciled on the call.
CFO transition: Subhadeep Pal takes over as CFO from 16 May 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the 15%+ growth outlook, but defensive on margins, cash flow reconciliation and opex increases. Management repeatedly attributed cost increases to revenue growth and one-offs, and gave limited quantification on market share and capex.
key_quotes: We are very confident of protecting the 11% and improving upon from here.
We are targeting to improve by 1% every year. And we believe that within the 2, 3 years, we should hit the 42%.
The capex is for a long term. And we have moved from INR800 crores revenue to INR1,600 crores, but the capex is designed for INR3,000 crores.

adds.what: Induction cooktop additional lines at Baddi (plus Bangalore) to reach 4-5 million units run-rate from ~2 million
IKEA three product lines, billing from Q1 FY27; INR200-250 crore revenue at full utilisation
Retail EBOs: 25 stores added per quarter to reach 500 by 2027 (329 at 31 March 2026)

growth.why: Management guides upwards of 15% FY27 revenue growth, backed by IKEA billing of INR40-50 crore by year-end from three awarded lines, induction lines at Baddi/Bangalore lifting capacity to 4-5 million units, and 25 EBOs per quarter; the induction and IKEA figures are specific but no order-value or line-commissioning dates are fully firmed up.
